title: [ConduitOS] Retain finite owner-bound CPL3 continuations for admitted preemption
body:
Parent #6184, under #6175. This is the missing native mechanism prerequisite, not the final two-service responsiveness proof.

Current x86_64 `ServiceDomain::enter` maps RTC budget expiry `(origin=2,value=4)` to `Fault(WorkExhausted)` and quarantines the owner. Timer interrupts may resume the current guest directly, but no interrupted guest context survives a return to Root for later scheduling. `ProtectedRegion`'s abstract `Preempted`/`Suspended` states do not supply that mechanism. Existing execution-region offers accurately advertise cooperative bounded steps.

Implement finite, private, owner-bound continuation custody in the existing protected-domain backend. Reuse existing `RegionBinding`, checked Plan/Play membership and protected-region transitions. Keep the final product scheduler/offer/fairness demonstration in #6184; do not introduce a scheduler, task/process ontology, proof round-robin or second runtime truth.

Acceptance:
- Capture a genuine CPL3 timer interruption before returning to Root; preserve the complete currently supported user GPR/interrupt-return state in admitted finite storage. Resume only the exact live Host/Boot/Plan/Play/region/service instance and mapped image/stack that owns that continuation. Root owns and validates return authority; guest-writable bytes cannot select arbitrary restore state.
- Distinguish a resumable scheduling slice from exhaustion of the admitted operation's total work grant. Remaining work is cumulative across resumes; resumption cannot replenish budget. Existing unsupported/one-shot callers retain terminal exhaustion. Do not weaken fault, cancellation, stale-instance, mapping, clock/FPU or port authority rules.
- Continuations have explicit single-use/replace/revoke transitions. Completion, fault, cancellation and release invalidate saved state before slot reuse; foreign, consumed, duplicate and prior-generation resume attempts refuse without affecting a sibling.
- Actual one-CPU native controls interrupt a real computation, return to Root, enter a distinct admitted CPL3 service, then resume the original computation at its saved point. Check supported registers/flags, exact identity, finite storage/budget, Root/sibling state, cumulative exhaustion and terminal cleanup. Keep FPU/XSAVE, physical/SMP and general fairness claims outside this mechanism proof.
- Hosted state/conformance controls and a supported source/ELF/ISO-bound native entrance accompany the change. Relevant Candidate and post-merge Integration pass before closure.

Existing seams: `targets/conduitos/src/{protected_region,execution_region,dual_region_kernel}.rs` and `targets/conduitos/src/arch/x86_64/{service_domain,domain_transition}.rs`. The real product integration must continue through existing `FixedScheduler` and checked execution regions, rather than a private fixture scheduler.

Ownership/admission: this board-sweep thread prepared the source audit. The entry/return surface is currently owned by #6308 (#6183); serialize implementation on that surface after its delivery. Retain #6184's #6176/#6181 dependency gates. Preparation here does not claim accepted preemptible execution or clear #6184's blocked status.



## Admission and context findings (2026-10-23)

The existing lane reservation, cooperative Step fuel and `maximum_work == 1` protected-entry limit do not define a cumulative hardware CPU grant. The RTC watchdog currently resets 16/64 ticks at every entry. The resumable profile must therefore bind a finite slice and cumulative limit into exact selected realization/Plan identity, with cumulative accounting **per admitted logical operation**, rather than capping an entire long-lived service. Resuming a slice must not renew that operation's grant; a subsequent legitimate request may receive its own grant only after the existing protocol owner establishes the prior terminal boundary. Retain the canonical RegionBinding and scheduler instead of adding a second grant/request authority. The exact selected-profile representation and protocol terminal boundary must be settled before assembly implementation.

A context limited to fifteen GPRs and RIP/RSP/RFLAGS would also be incomplete: CPL3 can change permitted/null data-segment selectors despite FSGSBASE being disabled. The context/entry policy must account for actual DS/ES/FS/GS selector and base state, the hardware interrupt frame and exact Root normalization before Rust, with no full-XSAVE/FPU authority extension. Preserve supported guest-visible state; validate/refuse unsupported state explicitly instead of silently resetting it. Existing #NM denial remains required on every resume. TF/debug, RF hardware-frame semantics and AC handling need explicit native controls. These findings are source audits, not new runtime failures or proof passes.

## Canonical policy prerequisite

#6317 owns the narrowly scoped canonical accounting policy, exact selected/fingerprinted identity, resource admission and existing-request operation boundary. The source audit found that no existing field grants this resumable cumulative policy; implement that explicit contract before enabling native resume. #6311 retains all actual CPL3 context/interrupt/cumulative/native controls, and #6184 retains the complete two-service product proof. Current core/native delivery ownership and the two-PR queue remain unchanged.



## Current isolated preparation (2026-10-24 UTC)

The old entry/return ownership hold has advanced: PR #6308 is merged and #6183 is closed. The canonical policy fields are delivered, but native capability-specific admission and actual owner/interrupt integration remain incomplete. The production command-custody prerequisite #6342 is in [PR #6365](https://github.com/dancxjo/conduit/pull/6365); it is now merged normally as `facf7e048cf4ee14f3a85d3aed4af8bedb7d5912`, with required Candidate checks passed and postmerge acceptance still tracked separately. The older preparation branch below remains source-qualified and does not silently absorb that merge.

Root has preserved an isolated preparation at [8114c57e53703d166781e1d4bde99a9bb401cf83](https://github.com/dancxjo/conduit/commit/8114c57e53703d166781e1d4bde99a9bb401cf83), branch `prep/6311-native-continuation-20261024`, based on development `dd92bde82017fe685404ef9197b56d3b3127006c`. It prepares the finite 192-byte supported machine-state representation, existing-binding/mapping/slice custody, and an exclusive source-timer qualification/counting seam. Default offers remain cooperative; no resumable native entry is enabled.

Six hosted controls pass with zero ignored (three custody, two clock count/refusal, one PIC decision), and workspace formatting passes. Both actual test executables and logs are retained. The compiled dirty-source snapshot is hash-matched to all ten prepared commit files; this is hosted preparation evidence, not native execution or full-feature acceptance. The initial external test-module path failure and formatting corrections remain recorded.

The clock preparation uses actual source IRQ qualification and refuses timer conflicts before token mutation; it does not reuse RTC ticks as accounting. Clock release currently quarantines its route against late untagged IRQs. Safe teardown/reuse and product timer coexistence remain unresolved, so this seam cannot yet support a general product offer.

Still required: actual pre-normalization IRQ capture, complete validated assembly restore, admitted concrete context backing and native selected-profile entry, cumulative accounting through the real request owner, terminal cleanup and real interrupted-service → Root → distinct admitted sibling → original-service resume controls. Retain the original full acceptance and #6184 product boundary. No implementation PR or completion claim is made from this preparation.



### Reviewed machine preparation (2026-10-24 UTC)

The same preparation branch now preserves [3f7ee5e8c1a5394f5b76cbbbd2f70a72c829564f](https://github.com/dancxjo/conduit/commit/3f7ee5e8c1a5394f5b76cbbbd2f70a72c829564f). Actual IRQ assembly spills the complete existing GPR/IRET frame and pre-normalization selectors/bases, normalizes Root state before Rust, and retains the captured user state for an in-place return. A separate IRET restore entry shares existing Root custody. A scoped single-entry sink remains occupied through owner drop; raw observations must pass existing binding/mapping/slice custody before a non-Copy immutable resume ticket can be used.

Both actual assembly variants (ordinary proof instrumentation off/on) compile for x86_64-unknown-none. Four hosted actual custody/sink controls pass at the final seven-file delta snapshot, and the earlier two clock plus one PIC controls pass on unchanged production source; formatting passes. Actual test executables and raw logs are retained, and all final delta hashes are matched to the prepared commit. This is assembly compilation and hosted state proof, not a whole native Rust/link build or native execution.

No default offer, ServiceDomain entry, RequestOwner accounting, selected-profile lowering or product scheduler activation is added. Full native Rust integration, charged backing, actual ongoing operation/new slice authorization, safe clock release/timer coexistence and the real interrupted A → Root → admitted B → resumed A controls remain required. The clock route retains its conservative poison-on-drop fallback; the teardown investigation produced no source change or reusable hardware-fence claim. No implementation PR or closure claim is made.



The preparation is now refreshed on development `7e9ccd0c6850d4f5782663f65ec7f5472109edb0` as [ec37536e34754873b4e679e348feb4a097447f12](https://github.com/dancxjo/conduit/commit/ec37536e34754873b4e679e348feb4a097447f12), branch `prep/6311-current-native-continuation-20261024`; both older recovery heads remain preserved. All fourteen owned preimages and resulting blobs were checked during the refresh, including the now-merged existing production request owner. At this exact clean prepared source, four actual hosted custody/sink tests and eleven production request-owner tests pass with zero ignored; both actual test executables and raw logs are retained. These hosted targets do not compile the target_os=none transition orchestration and do not prove native execution.

This issue remains `triage:blocked`: safely releasing the exclusive Source-clock route and preserving normal Host timer behavior remains unresolved. No further teardown iteration or profile activation follows from these hosted controls. Full native Rust/link integration, resource admission, actual ongoing operation/slice wiring and the original real A → Root → B → A controls remain required. The board sweep continues with ready deliveries while this concrete blocker remains.
